q-48721.name: Question 1
q-48721.problem:
For the function $f(x)$ and $g(x)$, you're given the following data:

$$
f(1)=2,\,{f}^{′}(1)=-3,\,g(1)=4,\,{g}^{′}(1)=2
$$

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))$ at $x=1.$
q-48721.worked_solution:
Using the product rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x)) & =f(x){g}^{′}(x)+g(x){f}^{′}(x).\end{aligned}
$$

At the point where $x=1$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(f(x)g(x))|}_{x=1} & =f(1){g}^{′}(1)+g(1){f}^{′}(1) \\  & =2\cdot 2+4\cdot (-3) \\  & =-8.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(x) & =-2{f}^{′}(x)(g(x)+1)+(-2f(x)-3){g}^{′}(x).\end{aligned}

At $x=2$, this gives

The quotient rule states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{u}{v})=\frac{{u}^{′}v-u{v}^{′}}{{v}^{2}}.
$$

Let $u=f(x)+1$ and $v=2g(x).$ Differentiating each, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}={f}^{′}(x)\,\text{and}\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=2{g}^{′}(x).
$$

Substituting this into the product rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(x) & =\frac{{u}^{′}v-u{v}^{′}}{{v}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{{f}^{′}(x)\cdot 2g(x)-(f(x)+1)\cdot 2{g}^{′}(x)}{{(2g(x))}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2{f}^{′}(x)g(x)-2{g}^{′}(x)(f(x)+1)}{4{g}^{2}(x)} \\  & =\frac{{f}^{′}(x)g(x)-{g}^{′}(x)(f(x)+1)}{2{g}^{2}(x)}.\end{aligned}
$$

At $x=2,$ this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(2) & =\frac{{f}^{′}(2)g(2)-{g}^{′}(2)(f(2)+1)}{2{g}^{2}(2)} \\  & =\frac{4\cdot 1-2(3+1)}{2\cdot {1}^{2}} \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$

$$
